items.title: F0-1: Prerender every indexable public route to its own document with its own title, description and canonical, and generate sitemap.xml from the same table
items.why: P0 THE SPINE (front-end architecture). GATE 0 must be green before P1 work starts.
items.dod: a no-JS fetch of each of the 13 indexable routes returns 13 different titles and 13 different absolute canonicals naming their own path, and sitemap.xml carries one loc per indexable route. Proven by a script that fetches every route and counts the distinct values on the deployed host — and by the same script against today's build showing 1 title and 4 locs. **Landed on the carrier 2026-10-20 and verified from the emitted files** (13 titles, 13 canonicals, 13 locs); the box waits for the deployed host, not for more code. items.key: f0-9 | p3 | the document carries the page's text, not only i
items.title: F0-9: The document carries the page's text, not only its head
items.why: P0 THE SPINE (front-end architecture). GATE 0 must be green before P1 work starts.
items.dod:
a no-JS fetch of the seven service pages and the homepage contains each page's own heading and its price text, proven by grepping the fetched HTML for a sentence that today exists only after JavaScript runs. Measured 2026-10-20 on the carrier's own build: `dist/screen-repair/index.html` had **bodyBytes=76, visibleTextChars=0**, because the generator rewrote the head and left `
` intact. **BUILT ON THE CARRIER, 2026-10-20, and measured:** the generator now renders each document's own page in a headless browser against a local server and writes the result inside `#root` — `/` 75 bytes/0 chars → **33,339 / 4,478**, `/screen-repair` → **11,477 / 2,039**, `/contact` → **18,562 / 2,111**, `/computer-finder` → **10,326 / 2,300**, every one of the 14 documents between 831 and 4,478 visible characters. With JavaScript disabled a browser now reads the real `

` and 2,018 body characters of the screen page. The capture waits for the page's own heading rather than a sleep, fails if the heading is absent, the deploy path fails the build on a missing browser or a failed capture while a plain build warns and leaves the document head-only, and `--check` goes red on a planted head-only document. The box waits for the deployed host, where the proof is a `curl`. **Still true after F1-6 and F1-7 landed: the carrier now also emits one JSON-LD graph per document with `Service.offers.price` matching the feed (118.66 on `/screen-repair`, and no `offers` at all on `/data-recovery`) and `openingHoursSpecification` generated from the same schedule module as the pages, proven by a planted-red test that moved a closing time to 18:00 and watched it fail.**

items.dod: a route change resets the scroll, an in-page anchor (`#faq`, `#contact`, a `/#…` deep link) still lands on its section, the back button still returns the customer where they were, and a test fails if the previous offset survives a navigation. **FOUND BY MEASUREMENT 2026-10-20, not by a test:** `frontend/scripts/journey-walk.mjs` tapped the Screen Repair card 2,926 px down the homepage, the route changed, and `/screen-repair` opened at `scrollY 2605` — its own maximum — with the price table **2,010 px above the viewport**. items.key: f1-2 | p3 | the public site quotes prices for its services,
items.title: F1-2: The public site quotes prices for its services, and it quotes them from the counter's own catalogue rather than from a literal typed into a component
items.why: P1 THE FRONT DOOR (the public site, which is the business). GATE 1 gates P2.
items.dod: all 7 service pages render a price table whose values come from one generated source, the same values appear on the pay page, and a test fails if a service page ships with no price row or types a dollar amount of its own. **CORRECTED TWICE, and the second correction is the useful one.** The old item assumed a pricing source existed to render from. My first pass then said none exists, because I looked in `device_services` and `model_parts` — **both empty**. The catalogue is `repair_parts`: **348 active priced rows across 73 models**, and it is provably the one the counter quotes from because it reproduces a published figure — iPhone 13 "Screen — Hard OLED" 54.32 + Tier 100.00 = **154.32**, the exact number the site was showing. It is now exported and transformed by `scripts/pricing/public-prices.sql` and `scripts/pricing/build-public-prices.mjs` into a committed feed: screen 33 models, battery 38, charging-port 33, laptop 19, flip-phone 13, and `data-recovery` and `tablet` with **none** — those two pages must say "quoted at the counter", not invent a number. **What still blocks a published price is not code: all 348 rows carry the SAME labour tier** ("Tier $100+", 100.00), so a $1.95 flex and a $113 OLED assembly both attract $100 of labour, and 6 rows have a part sell price of 0 that is an unconfigured cost rather than a free part (the builder drops them). That is owner queue **#867**. The box stays unticked until the pages render from the feed and the pricing policy question is answered. **BUILT ON THE CARRIER 2026-10-20:** four service pages render a table from the feed (`/screen-repair` 33 rows, `/battery-replacement` 38, `/laptop-repair` 19, `/kosher-flip-phones` 13; eight shown, cheapest first), `/phone-repair` shows a single feed-derived from-line rather than presenting one repair category as its whole price list, and `/data-recovery` and `/tablet-repair` say in words that they are quoted per job at the counter because the catalogue has no priced rows for them. A guard test fails on any dollar amount on those pages that is not from the feed, proven red by planting "$999.99". And the prices are now in the **document**, not only in the browser: a no-JS fetch of `/screen-repair` carries `$118.66 $130.79 $135.00`.

items.key: f1-3 | p3 | the shop's hours are stated once and rendered ev
items.title: F1-3: The shop's hours are stated once and rendered everywhere from that one source
items.why: P1 THE FRONT DOOR (the public site, which is the business). GATE 1 gates P2.
items.dod: the homepage, the footer, the contact page and the FAQ render hours generated from the same schedule, Saturday-closed and the Friday cutoff appear wherever a customer could act on them, and a contract test fails if any surface types its own hours sentence. **Landed on the carrier 2026-10-20 and it exposed the real defect underneath:** the four surfaces now render from `features/settings/shopHours.ts:getShopHoursLines()`, and doing it revealed that the FAQ's *"Fridays until 1.5 hours before sunset"* describes a rule **the schedule does not implement** — `backend/src/lib/business-hours.ts:69` makes Friday drop-off-only and no sunset rule exists anywhere in the tree. So one of the four disagreements was the site claiming *more* than the shop does. Which one is true is the shop's rule, not a code question: **owner queue #863** asks whether Friday takes walk-ins until 1.5 h before sunset or is drop-off only all day. The box stays unticked until that is answered and the schedule carries the true rule — at which point one edit reaches all four surfaces, which is the point of the change.

items.key: l1-2 | p3 | every filter means what its label says, proven f
items.title: L1-2: Every filter means what its label says, proven from the request it produces
items.why: P2 THE LOGIC (reach and truth in search). GATE 2 gates P3.
items.dod: a sweep lists every control on the staff surfaces whose label promises more than it does and every search box whose scope is invisible, and each one is either proven to mean what its words say with the request quoted from the code path, or fixed and re-proved. A tick without that list is a claim about screens nobody looked at. The recency-window half of this theme is already fixed (#499) — re-read the source before repeating any older claim. **Swept on the carrier 2026-10-20: 43 controls — 37 TRUTHFUL, 1 NARROWED, 1 INVISIBLE-SCOPE, 4 NEED A DECISION; after the fixes 39 are truthful. The narrowed one was the owner's own screen: the Work Orders hub sent `[AWAITING_DIAGNOSIS, AWAITING_APPROVAL, AWAITING_PARTS]` for `All statuses` — three of seven — and now sends all seven, proven by a test that fails when the preset is reverted. The prior sweep (2026-10-14) covered 16 controls and **missed the Work Orders hub entirely**, which is exactly the "claim about screens nobody looked at" this item warned about. Four controls still need a product decision rather than a fix: receipts `All Statuses` (the endpoint throws before any `where`), `ConversationSearch All Types` (unmounted), profit analytics `All Categories` (the value is never consumed), inventory `All Device Types` (never sent, and the server schema has no such field). **All four settled the same night, as engineering calls with tests:** receipts hidden behind the feature's own availability (the endpoint throws before any `where`), `ConversationSearch` removed (no importer), profit analytics removed (the value was never read and the component already holds every category), inventory removed (no wire, no schema field). Result: **43 controls inspected, 39 on screen, 39 TRUTHFUL, 0 NARROWED, 0 INVISIBLE-SCOPE, 0 NEEDS-A-DECISION**, with a guard that fails when a new `All …`/`Both`/`Every`/`Any` control appears without a line that sends its value — proven red by planting `All Warehouses`.**

items.key: l1-3 | p4 | every list can reach the record it is hiding | d
items.title: L1-3: Every list can reach the record it is hiding
items.why: P2 THE LOGIC (reach and truth in search). GATE 2 gates P3.
items.dod: a sweep of the staff-facing lists finds every surface that truncates without a way to page, and each one either pages with the page size and the total shown or is proven not to truncate. Proven by a count of lists before and after, and by one real record reached that was previously unreachable. **Swept on the carrier 2026-10-20: 18 staff-facing lists — 10 REACHABLE, 6 TRUNCATES-WITHOUT-REACH, 2 UNKNOWN. Three fixed with the existing `ListPager` (work-order hub 500-row cap replaced, staff issues pinned at 100, payments transactions pinned at 100); the other six are reported with the server-side gap that blocks each, because a pager over a query that cannot offset is decoration. A guard fails on a new literal `limit:`/`take:` in the staff tree with no reach mechanism, proven red by planting one.** **Completed to 15 of 18 on 2026-10-20:** five of the six gaps got `offset` and `total` (collections, repair intake, pricing config history, counter case activity, payments overview), the audit was corrected where its own reasoning had been wrong (`order.service.ts:619-681` already read every eligible order and filtered in memory, so Collections needed no data-layer change at all), and the one remaining truncation is the counter queue, which needs one ordering across two sources rather than two offsets. Closing the gaps surfaced a real regression the carrier caught: the new `id` tie-breaker in `getConfigHistory` made two assertions stale, and the backend suite went 1 -> 3 failures against a clean `origin/test` baseline of 1. Both assertions now pin the stable order, because paging over a non-unique key can repeat or skip a boundary row.

items.key: u4-2 | p2 | the money on a job says what the shop is actuall
items.title: U4-2: The money on a job says what the shop is actually charging, and the tax is added unless a person says otherwise
items.dod: an order with no price set can never display a computed number as its quote (the 75-quoted / 70.34-charged case is reproduced as a test), `Sales tax included` defaults to **unchecked** on both the work order and the sale, the sentence beside the figure always matches the checkbox, and a deposit can be recorded against a job as an amount with a running balance — or the schema change that blocks it is named. Proven by tests asserting the exact strings. **The arithmetic is already closed, 2026-10-20:** 75 / 1.06625 = 70.34 — the quote was read as tax-inclusive and stored as its net base, and 65.97 + 4.37 in the Charge block is 70.34 / 1.06625. The shortfall is **4.66 per job if 75 meant the customer pays 75, and 9.63 if it meant 75 plus tax** — owner queue **#874** asks which, because that is a money rule, not code.

items.key: u4-6 | p3 | the computer finder asks the questions a person
items.title: U4-6: The computer finder asks the questions a person can answer, and says less
items.dod: CF-1 to CF-9 are each resolved and the landing page leads with the two facts that matter (the $75 down payment and the $500 floor), the use-case, portability, screen-size and condition options match CF-3 to CF-6, every page carries a free-text note box, the budget list loses the option the shop refuses, and the contact checkbox says "please call me" because text is the default. Proven by the walk's assertions, not by reading the diff. **BUILT 2026-10-20: the landing page went from 297 visible words to 80 and leads with the $75 down payment and the $500 floor; "Windows licence included" is gone; Q2 opens with "Offline work — writing, documents, no internet"; Q3 gains "I'm not sure" and asks about weight and how often the machine moves; Q4 becomes 13.3 / 14 / 15.6-16 / 17+; "nobody used it" becomes "less used than new, already opened"; every question page carries an optional notes box that survives going back and is appended to what the shop receives; the sub-$500 budget option is gone; and the contact checkbox now reads "Please call me — don't text". The gap that was flagged at build time is closed the same night: the call-me preference now reaches the notification itself — `buildComputerRequestSmsBody` adds "The customer asked to be called — do not text them." above the note, so the one place a person acts on it says so. Two tests pin it (18 in that suite).**

items.title: U4-7: A computer request reaches the shop, and cannot be lost
items.dod: a submission sends a text to the shop through the live sender, appears in a staff queue, and a failed send leaves the row FAILED with its reason and a retry — proven by tests for the happy path, the failure path and a double submit producing one text. **Built 2026-10-20; the deployed backend needs `DIALPAD_API_KEY` or every send fails closed with a visible reason.**

items.key: u4-5 | p3 | the walk itself becomes an instrument | done whe
items.title: U4-5: **The walk itself becomes an instrument**
items.dod: `frontend/scripts/owner-walk.mjs` replays the fifteen steps above against a local build and fails on any of them regressing — a cold-load budget, one spinner, no overlapping boxes, one clear button, visible text while typing, `New` landing on the intake, the tax box unchecked by default, a red marker on every required field, a tile that filters — and it is wired so a shift runs it after the personas. **A defect found by a human walking the product must become a check, or the next human walks it again.** **BUILT 2026-10-20, same night: `frontend/scripts/owner-walk.mjs` replays ten of the twenty-five as assertions and passes — a cold-load budget with the request and duplicate counts, exactly one loading indicator, zero overlap between panels at 1280 and 393, each summary tile applying its own filter, exactly one clear control with the input at least 120 px wide, `New` landing on the intake, a required marker on every required field, a typed 180 charging 191.93 with the tax box unchecked, a photo rendered on the job, and sign-out surviving the Back button. Three of the ten were proven able to fail by planting the defect at runtime. Not yet checked: the deposit flow, the issue-text hierarchy, the finder's ten, and a real production load — and it is not yet wired into a scheduler, which is what keeps the box unticked.**

items.key: d1-1 | p3 | the ledger and the roadmap reconcile with each o
items.title: D1-1: The ledger and the roadmap reconcile with each other, automatically, in both directions
items.why: P4 THE LAST MILE (delivery). GATE 4 is never finished; it is held.
items.dod: a read-only reconciler reports as one line the ledger items open whose PR has merged, the boxes ticked whose ledger item is still open, and the boxes unchecked whose ledger item closed with proof — and its first run closes the known drifts (items 740 and 724; boxes for #380, #452, #13, #107, #108, #109), or names why not. **A first version is installed and running, 2026-10-20:** `/root/bin/lpt-reconcile.py` with `lpt-reconcile.timer` every 3 h at :47 (`--fix-safe --refresh-checkout`). Its first live run found ledger item **488 open although `39d58a847` was already an ancestor of `origin/test`**, and closed it with the merge as its proof — proven on a copy of `work.db` first, after fixing a real trap: `work.py` writes its default database unless told otherwise, so the copy run would have closed a production row. It reports D2 and D3 and auto-fixes neither. **It also found the loop's own input was stale:** `roadmap-supply` runs `docs=local` and that checkout was on a DETACHED HEAD from 2026-10-19 (`a6b572bf9`) carrying ten uncommitted files whose content is identical to the merged #499 — so a roadmap merged into `origin/test` would never have reached the loop, while every surface read healthy. The timer now refreshes that checkout (refusing on uncommitted tracked changes), with the old state archived and stashed. This box stays unticked until the D2/D3 counts reach zero.
